title: Construct near-unit rational Stein generators: factor 9/8 (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped proof and exact coefficient producer. Replace PR4198's factor-two rational Stein-generator normalization by an arbitrary requested factor `1+2^-p`, with the same exact rank-many terms and at most `p+2` additional height bits per rational component.

```diff
 E = sum_j g_j a_j,  ||g_j||_2 <= 1
-||a_j||_2 < 2 ||E||_2
+||a_j||_2 < (1+2^-p) ||E||_2
+p=3 gives the concrete bound 9/8
```

The normalizer uses integer square root and exact squared comparisons. A rank-one example proves that exact factor one can fail over Q(i) when the term count must remain minimal. On that example the new squared row norm is `49/16`, versus `4` from the old power-of-two formula. These are newly computed formula evaluations, not a predecessor replay. No new kappa or selected-frontier change.

[Proof and package](https://github.com/petalas/integer-mult-bounds/tree/d85df7f7524e41799a6db2d6c082f6cadbd5cc84/research/near-unit-stein-normalization). This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Credit Jose Manuel / jmbarrancoml's PR4198 at `e457d5e912a27307d725827aeca7198169320b84` for the rational orthogonal-residual factorization, coefficient-row convention and interface; Vlado Vojdanovski / PR1673 for the dirty-shear compiler; Cinna Davis and the retained caller/phase lineage. Gram-Schmidt, integer square root and the norm obstruction are classical.

## Evidence

All checks pass locally on CPython 3.12.15, macOS arm64, using only the standard library:

- 4,800 independent exponent/mantissa-oracle comparisons on 960 rational squared norms; 84 wide-exponent/precision normalizers.
- 717 real/complex matrix fixtures, all 2,151 factorizations at p=1,3,9, and 3,645 emitted terms. Separate row elimination checks rank; complete reconstruction, residual orthogonality and exact Hermitian PSD certificates check the row-norm inequality.
- Eighteen explicit domain/semantic controls. Three disposable mutations, round-down, wrong conjugation and tiny-term deletion, reject. Actual pinned-proof corruption also rejects under optimized execution.
- Warning-strict normal and optimized direct checks produce identical hash-bound receipts and take 0.519 s and 0.528 s locally. Both registered commands pass, with a 120-second limit each. These durations establish replay budget only.
- Seven-file committed-byte/mode/source-history preflight and official export integrity pass. Both modes pass with Git absent and exported files read-only; all eight export files retain their bytes and modes.

From the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/near-unit-stein-normalization/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/near-unit-stein-normalization/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/near-unit-stein-normalization
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/near-unit-stein-normalization --check-source-history --check-modes
```

Any CPython 3.12 path can replace the local interpreter. Expected markers are `PASS_NEAR_UNIT_STEIN_NORMALIZATION`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`. The default verifier is read-only and Git-free; optional `--receipt PATH` creates a source-hash-bound receipt without overwriting an existing file.

## Limitations

The universal theorem is the written proof, not finite extrapolation or proof-kernel acceptance. The supplied producer enforces dimension <=8, input component height <=512, precision 1..128 and a 65,536-bit normalizer capacity, rejecting exhaustion. The mathematical proof has arbitrary finite dimension and precision. The scale is dyadic; the resulting Gaussian-rational coefficients can have odd denominators.

No rounded FFT/triangular child, actual coefficient delivery, physical precision saving, complete dirty-state error ledger, full caller/stock/tape invoice, supplier admission or multiplication theorem is supplied. All five inherited framework assumptions remain. No predecessor executable, historical scientific suite, Lean or selected cold replay was run. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Open next questions

Can one actual rounded Gaussian child exploit the smaller coefficient norms? Bind one emitted row and its normalizer to the literal coefficient/data rounding and allocation contract, then charge delivery and physical costs. Those interfaces remain missing; no implementation expansion is claimed here.

## Related open work

No other open PR studying this exact rational Stein normalization was found in the complete cached open-PR corpus and refreshed live list. PR4198 is the merged predecessor. The live mathematical claims concern P104 label geometry, temporal rails, helper cuts, native coframes and coding rather than this normalization. The separate encoded Gaussian-inverse setup optimization preserves a different calculation and computes no competing normalization constant.

Door: two-way. Blast radius: isolated. Six new files in one opt-in package. No shared implementation, frozen source or selected record changes.
